text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended the day with pared gains tracking early losses on nearby New York contracts. Benchmark September slipped from a high of $1,617 per tonne to end the day $18 lower at $1,578, well below the psychologically important $1,600 mark. Origin selling and price fixing from Africa and Indonesia capped the gains. Traders expect robusta futures to consolidate around current levels after Tuesday's sell off which took September to a six month low of $1,477.

Arabica futures in New York finished mixed, with the September contract posting modest losses but ending well off session lows. By the close September stood at 180.40 cents/lb, down 1.25 cents on the day while second position December rose 2.15 cents/lb, to 160.30 cents/lb. The back months closed up 1.00 to 3.90. The focus is still on the amount of coffee deliverable against September which is considered to be extremely low relative to the open interest. Further down the road there seems to be some concern about dryness in parts of Central America and the impact this might have on the 1997/98 output. If crops should be below recent expectations, tight supplies of high quality coffees could be the result, analysts said.

UNITED STATES - The CSCE reported certified coffee stocks dipped by 252 60-kg bags as of July 23, to 90,645 bags. An additional 1,489 bags were pending grading, the Exchange said. Of the 4,120 bags graded 2,683 bags passed Exchange approval.

DENMARK - Coffee imports in April 1997 amounted to 105,009 60-kg bags, up from 85,695 bags in April 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first four months of 1997 (January/April) up to 365,734 bags, up 6 per cent on the tonnage imported in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1996 reached 1.008 million bags compared to 873,675 bags in 1995. Major suppliers of green coffee in 1997 were Brazil (158,700 vs 85,300 bags), Colombia (62,200 vs 79,900 bags) and Mexico (17,700 vs 5,900 bags).

Coffee exports in April 1997 amounted to 11,966 bags which brought cumulative exports in January/April 1997 up to 47,113 bags against 31,914 bags in 1996. Total exports in 1996 reached 108,096 bags, up from 91,166 bags in 1995. Denmark exports most of its coffee in the form of roast and ground with Latvia (7,600 vs 5,900 bags) and Germany (6,400 vs 2,200 bags) being the main markets.

ROMANIA - Coffee imports in February 1997 amounted to 14,900 bags, which brought cumulative imports in the first months of 1997 (January/February) up to 48,150 bags against 28,667 bags in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1996 amounted to 467,233 bags against 243,200 bags in 1995. Major suppliers of green coffee in 1997 were Indonesia (26,100 vs 16,600 bags) and Brazil (10,300 vs 5,500 bags).
